title: Green Guardian: Save the Forest
description: Protect precious forest habitats from reckless development! Place conservation zones to shield wildlife corridors and old-growth forests while developers try to clear land for construction. Every move teaches real environmental science — from ecosystem balance and biodiversity to conservation strategy and habitat connectivity.
learning_objectives: Understand why forests and natural habitats need protection from development
Learn how wildlife corridors connect habitats and support biodiversity
Practice thinking about ecosystems as interconnected territories
Explore the tension between economic development and environmental conservation
Develop spatial reasoning about how protected areas create safe zones for wildlife
Understand the concept of buffer zones and why surrounding habitat matters
how_to_play: You and the AI take turns placing markers on a 9x9 wilderness grid. You place Protected Forest zones; the AI places Development projects.
Surround empty intersections with your protected forests to claim that territory as a nature reserve — safe habitat for wildlife!
If you completely surround a cluster of Development markers (no empty adjacent spaces), those projects are shut down — conservation victory!
The Ko rule prevents you from immediately re-protecting a zone that was just cleared, simulating the time nature needs to recover.
The game ends when both sides pass consecutively, meaning the land-use map is settled.
Your score is protected habitat plus developments you stopped. The developers get a 6.5 point komi head start. Save more forest than they can clear to win!

storybook_pages.title: The Forest Needs You
storybook_pages.text: A beautiful wilderness stretches across the grid — home to deer, owls, foxes, and countless other creatures. But a big development company wants to bulldoze the land for shopping malls, parking lots, and highways. As the Green Guardian, you must place protected forest zones to save as much habitat as possible before it's too late.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: lush green forest viewed from above forming a 9x9 grid, woodland animals peeking out, bulldozers approaching from one side, a child in a green cape standing protectively, bright cartoon style for kids

storybook_pages.title: Connect the Wild
storybook_pages.text: Animals don't just need one patch of forest — they need connected habitats to roam, hunt, and find mates. When you place protected zones next to each other, you create wildlife corridors that let creatures move safely. But if developers cut through your corridors, animals get trapped in tiny islands of forest. Think about connections, not just individual spots!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: colorful illustrated map showing connected green forest zones with animals traveling between them through corridors, some areas blocked by construction with sad animals, educational kids cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Every Tree Counts
storybook_pages.text: As the grid fills up, the stakes get higher. Some areas might be lost to development, but you can still save the heart of the forest. Sometimes protecting a key corridor is more important than saving a distant patch. Think like a real conservationist — prioritize the areas that matter most for the whole ecosystem.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: dramatic split view of the grid showing a thriving protected forest with happy animals on one side and cleared development land on the other, a scoreboard showing habitat saved, hopeful sunset, kids cartoon style

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: India hosts 4 of the 36 global biodiversity hotspots and faces intense pressure on its natural ecosystems from development. Conservation strategy thinking is increasingly relevant for India's environmental governance.
reflection_prompt: Where did you trade influence for territory? Was it worth it?
